newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs pare gains on report of EPA rate rise comment.
newsitem.headline: JGBs pare gains on report of EPA rate rise comment.

text.p: Key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures ended down on Monday due to a wire service report which quoted a government minister as saying interest rates may rise by the end of the year.
Traders said a wire service report quoted Economic Planning Agency Minister Taro Aso as saying a rise in the official discount rate is very possible by the end of the year.
Aso was also quoted as saying that a decision on the official discount rate is up to the Bank of Japan.
Before Aso's comments were reported, JGBs had been firm due to a fall in Tokyo share prices, traders said.
The September was last traded at 126.47, down from Friday's close of 126.67. Turnover was 36,910 contracts.

An offer worth 300 million yen came in at 126.41 after the September was traded at 126.47, but it could not be evenly distributed among standing bids so would be carried over to Tuesday's morning session, an official of the Tokyo Stock Exchange said.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.110 percent as of 0638 GMT, up slightly from Friday's close of 2.105 percent.
Earlier, the benchmark JGB yield fell to a record low of 2.070 percent due to a weakness in Tokyo share prices.
Scattered buying of cash bonds by investors was detected, a city bank trader said.
"But they are not buying very aggressively right now. Most investors want to buy at a level half a point to a full point lower than current levels," he said.
Regarding the reported rate-rise comments by the EPA minister, traders said that the impact on Japanese debt markets may be short-lived.
"The BOJ's latest quarterly economic report was very weak, and I don't think the EPA minister's remarks mean there will be an immediate interest-rate rise," the city bank trader said.

Aso, asked in an exclusive interview with Dow Jones about the possibility that Japanese interest rates could rise by the end of the year, was quoted as saying that the discount rate had remained at a record low 0.5 percent for nearly two years and added: "It should be higher than now; It's very possible. That's all I can say at this moment."
Asked why the discount rate might have risen by then, Aso said: "The economy will have grown by then." Aso also emphasised that any decision on the rate was up to the BOJ.
In the morning session, JGBs were sold initially, but later recovered due to falls in share prices, traders said.
JGBs were sold initially due to a sharp fall in U.S. Treasury bonds on Friday, traders said.

On the recent weakness in Tokyo share prices, traders said there has been speculation in the market since last week that an American investment bank has been reducing its holdings in Tokyo stocks in preparation for a scaling back of its Asian operations.
But traders said the impact of such rumours on the JGB market had been limited so far.
